name: Equiv.Perm.sign_eq_prod_prod_Ioi
script:
intro h
have h₁ := h (n := 0)
have h₂ : Equiv.Perm.sign (Equiv.refl (Fin 0)) = ∏ i : Fin 0, ∏ j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, if (Equiv.refl (Fin 0) : Equiv.Perm (Fin 0)) i < (Equiv.refl (Fin 0) : Equiv.Perm (Fin 0)) j then 1 else -1 := by
  simpa using h₁ (σ := Equiv.refl (Fin 0))
have h₃ : ∏ i : Fin 0, ∏ j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, if (Equiv.refl (Fin 0) : Equiv.Perm (Fin 0)) i < (Equiv.refl (Fin 0) : Equiv.Perm (Fin 0)) j then 1 else -1 = 1 := by
  simp [Finset.prod_const]
have h₄ : Equiv.Perm.sign (Equiv.refl (Fin 0)) = 1 := by
  simpa using h₂.trans h₃
have h₅ : Equiv.Perm.sign (Equiv.refl (Fin 0)) = 1 := by
  simpa using h₄
have h₆ : Equiv.Perm.sign (Equiv.refl (Fin 0)) = -1 := by
  -- This is a contradiction because the sign of the identity permutation is 1, not -1.
  -- However, we need to adjust our approach since we are using a different definition in Lean.
  have h₇ : Equiv.Perm.sign (Equiv.refl (Fin 0)) = 1 := by
    simpa using h₄
  simp_all [Equiv.Perm.sign]
  <;> aesop
-- Contradiction arises as the sign of the identity permutation cannot be both 1 and -1.
simp_all

script:
intro h
have h₁ := h (α := PUnit) (M := ⟨∅, by simp⟩) (N := ⟨∅, by simp⟩)

  intro h₄

  have h₅ : (⟨∅, by simp⟩ : Matroid PUnit) <m (⟨∅, by simp⟩ : Matroid PUnit) → False := by
    intro h₆
    -- This is a contradiction because a set cannot be less than itself.
    exact lt_irrefl _ h₆
  exact h₅ h₄

  tauto

name: MeasurableSpace.measurableSet_bot_iff
script:
intro h
have h₁ : ∀ {α : Type u_1} {s : Set α}, MeasurableSet s ↔ s = ∅ ∨ s = Set.univ := h
-- We will derive a contradiction by considering the measurable set ℝ in the real numbers.
have h₂ : (Set.Iio (0 : ℝ) : Set ℝ) ≠ ∅ := by
  intro h₃
  have h₄ : (0 : ℝ) < 1 := by norm_num
  have h₅ : (Set.Iio (0 : ℝ)) = ∅ := h₃
  have h₆ : (1 : ℝ) ∈ Set.Iio (0 : ℝ) := by
    rw [h₅]
    exact Set.mem_empty_iff_false.mpr (by norm_num)
  norm_num at h₆
have h₃ : ¬((Set.Iio (0 : ℝ) : Set ℝ) = ∅ ∨ (Set.Iio (0 : ℝ) : Set ℝ) = Set.univ) := by
  intro h₄
  cases h₄ with
  | inl h₄ =>
    exact h₂ h₄
  | inr h₄ =>
    have h₅ : (1 : ℝ) ∈ Set.Iio (0 : ℝ) := by
      rw [h₄]
      norm_num
    norm_num at h₅
have h₄ : MeasurableSet (Set.Iio (0 : ℝ)) ↔ (Set.Iio (0 : ℝ) : Set ℝ) = ∅ ∨ (Set.Iio (0 : ℝ) : Set ℝ) = Set.univ := by
  apply h₁
have h₅ : ¬MeasurableSet (Set.Iio (0 : ℝ)) := by
  intro h₆
  have h₇ : (Set.Iio (0 : ℝ) : Set ℝ) = ∅ ∨ (Set.Iio (0 : ℝ) : Set ℝ) = Set.univ := by
    exact h₄.mp h₆
  exact h₃ h₇
-- We have a contradiction because the interval (-∞, 0) is measurable in the real numbers.
have h₆ : MeasurableSet (Set.Iio (0 : ℝ)) := by
  apply Set.measurable_Iio
exact h₅ h₆
